# Summary of the Cairn System

## Basic Concepts

A cairn is a structure with a height measured in marks. The system involves several operations that change its height.

## Pulses

A pulse is a growth event. When you pulse a cairn, it grows by the stride amount plus a bonus based on its current size.

The calculation: Take the current height, add the stride, then add however many complete strides fit into the original height (using integer division).

Key point: Taller cairns grow more from each pulse because more full strides fit inside them.

## Multiple Pulses

When applying several pulses in sequence, you must recalculate after each one. You can't just multiply by the number of pulses—each pulse depends on the height at that moment.

## Leaks

A leak is a loss that happens after a pulse. It removes marks proportional to the pulsed height. For every full group of (leak size) marks in the pulsed height, one mark is lost.

## Drains

Unlike leaks, a drain removes a fixed number of marks after every pulse. As the cairn shrinks, the pulse adds less (since stride count decreases), but the drain stays constant. Eventually the cairn can empty.

## Finding Origins

To find the starting height before pulses were applied, work backwards. For each pulse, find what height would produce the current height when pulsed with that stride.

## Merging

Two cairns combine into one using weighted shares (expressed in tenths) plus a fixed tether value. Apply each share to get marks from each cairn (using floor function), then add the tether.
